name: Orange Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: powdered white sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of powdered white sugar

ingredients.name: wine-glass of mixed wine and brandy
ingredients.originalText: a wine-glass of mixed wine and brandy

instructions.text: Grate the yellow part of the rind, and squeeze the juice of the oranges.
Stir together to a cream half a pound of butter, and half a pound of powdered white sugar, and add a wine-glass of mixed wine and brandy.
Beat very light six eggs, and stir them gradually into the mixture.
Put it into a buttered dish with a broad edge, round which lay a border of puff-paste neatly notched.
Bake it half an hour, and when cool grate white sugar over it.
Send it to table quite cold.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Grate the yellow part of the rind, and squeeze the juice of the oranges.
2. Stir together to a cream half a pound of butter, and half a pound of powdered white sugar, and add a wine-glass of mixed wine and brandy.
3. Beat very light six eggs, and stir them gradually into the mixture.
4. Put it into a buttered dish with a broad edge, round which lay a border of puff-paste neatly notched.
5. Bake it half an hour, and when cool grate white sugar over it.
6. Send it to table quite cold.
